title: Rewarding Graph Reasoning Process makes LLMs more Generalized Reasoners

problem.claim: Developing advanced reasoning capabilities in LLMs remains challenging.

gap.claim: Applying process reward models to broader reasoning domains is understudied because manually creating step-level supervision is costly.

contributions.claim: GraphSilo is a graph reasoning dataset with fine-grained step-wise labels generated using automated task-oriented trajectories and MCTS.
GraphPRM is a process reward model designed for graph reasoning problems.
The work evaluates GraphPRM through inference-time scaling and reinforcement learning via DPO.

author_reported_evidence.claim: GraphPRM reportedly improves LLM performance across 13 graph reasoning tasks, including a 9% gain for Qwen2.5-7B, and transfers to new graph reasoning datasets and mathematical problem-solving.
GraphPRM reportedly improves performance on GSM8K and MATH500.

narrative_sequence.summary: Advanced reasoning in LLMs remains a key challenge, while PRMs have shown promise mainly for mathematical reasoning.
Broader PRM applications are limited by the cost of manually producing step-level supervision.
The work applies PRMs to graph reasoning and uses graph algorithms to automate step-level data generation.
The authors introduce GraphSilo and train GraphPRM, evaluating it with inference-time scaling and DPO.
The authors report gains across graph tasks and transfer benefits to mathematical reasoning datasets and domains.

source_observation.claim: Automated trajectories and MCTS are used to generate fine-grained step-wise labels for graph reasoning.

interpretation.claim: Algorithmic supervision generation may reduce the manual cost of training process reward models in structured reasoning domains.

application.claim: For another structured multi-step reasoning domain, investigate whether domain algorithms can produce labeled reasoning trajectories for PRM training.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that automated labels are reliable across domains or tasks.

source_observation.claim: GraphPRM reportedly improves graph reasoning and mathematical problem-solving performance.

interpretation.claim: Process rewards learned in one structured reasoning domain may transfer beyond that domain.

application.claim: Evaluate domain-specific process rewards on both in-domain tasks and carefully selected out-of-domain reasoning tasks.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the transfer conditions, baselines, or whether the reported gains generalize beyond the stated datasets.

unknowns: GraphSilo size, composition, and task distribution are unspecified.
Baseline models, evaluation metrics, statistical details, and experimental settings are unspecified.
The exact transfer setup and contributions of inference-time scaling versus DPO are unspecified.
